name: Supertouch
label: Revelation
lede: Supertouch put funk, quiet parts and major chords into late-'80s New York hardcore, fronted by a b-boy singer and named after a Bad Brains song. The scene mostly wanted mosh parts, and the band never got the credit.

eras.title: From Death Before Dishonor to a Bad Brains song title
eras.text: Mark Ryan and Jon Biviano started out as Death Before Dishonor, with Mike Ferraro on drums when he was around. When Ferraro left for Youth of Today, the pair found a new drummer, a new bassist and a name from a Bad Brains song.

years.h: Mark Ryan starts Death Before Dishonor in New York
years.p: Ryan recruits Jon Biviano, on bass at first, and the two form the band. [[Mike Ferraro|edffc714-f0a2-4d6c-b4c0-dc31e713481c]], later of [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]], plays drums when he can. Revelation dates Supertouch from here.
years.xp: Biviano says he was kicked out after two or three practices, then came back as the guitarist.

years.h: Two gigs with Schreifels on bass, then the drummer walks
years.p: With [[Mike Ferraro|edffc714-f0a2-4d6c-b4c0-dc31e713481c]] on drums and [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]], soon of [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]], on bass, the band plays two shows in spring 1987. Then Ferraro joins [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]].
years.xp: Biviano's account says Ferraro's move to Youth of Today caused real tension in the New York scene.

years.cap: Supertouch's singer in the crowd at the Anthrax, Norwalk, Connecticut, around 1987
years.src: RevHQ: Jon Biv Part IV · Revelation Records
years.h: A drummer from a dead band, and a name from Bad Brains
years.p: Mark Ryan finds Andy Guida, whose band Altercation had just folded, and Mike Bitton takes bass. Named after a [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] song, Supertouch is official by September 1987.
years.xp:
Biviano says Guida clicked at once: the new line-up got more done in two hours than in two years with Ferraro. Guida had "issues with the scene" that matched the band's own.

By fall 1987 they were writing what nobody else in hardcore was. In Biviano's words, "we weren't afraid to add in quiet parts." Revelation's own bio singles out Ryan as one of hardcore's first b-boys, alongside Eddie Sutton of [[Leeway|121193a5-cb8b-4182-968c-8ba607856fa2]].

eras.title: Grooves nobody else in New York had
eras.text: Supertouch played quiet sections, major chords and funk-born improvisation for a crowd that wanted mosh parts. One 7" and one Revelation album caught it, and the band's WNYU tape spread through the trading underground.

years.cap: Flyer for a Sunday matinee at the Rocket, Providence, March 20, with Underdog and Raw Deal, 1988
years.h: Seven songs live on WNYU, nearly all of them unreleased
years.p: On St. Patrick's Day 1988, Mark Ryan, Jon Biviano, Andy Guida and Mike Bitton play Crucial Chaos. Only Climbing Aboard later turns up on a Supertouch record.
years.xp:
Crucial Chaos ran Thursdays, 9 to 10:30 p.m. The set included Searching for the Light, True Colors Don't Run and Death in the Family.

A friend taped the broadcast off his home stereo, and the tape circulated among traders for two decades before Horror Hotel pressed it on vinyl in 2011. In Effect calls it the best document of the original line-up.

years.h: A first spot on a Revelation comp, next to Youth of Today
years.p: Searchin' for the Light lands on Revelation's New York City Hardcore: The Way It Is, alongside [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]].

years.h: A Village Voice ad finds the new bassist
years.p: With Mike Bitton out, Joe Graz answers the ad and learns all ten songs on the Supertouch demo before his audition, so it's barely a tryout at all.

years.h: Supertouch's first record is a 7" on Combined Effort
years.p: What Did We Learn is the one record between the WNYU tapes and the Revelation album.
years.xp: The 7" carries Climbing Aboard, the only song from the 1988 WNYU set that Supertouch ever put on a record.

years.cap: Flyer for Hardcore Benefit III for Amnesty International, the Ritz, New York, August 10, 1990
years.h: Two benefit shows in one day: Newark matinee, Connecticut night
years.p: Jon Biviano recalls playing the Pipeline in Newark for radio station WFMU, then the Anthrax in Norwalk for Amnesty International.
years.xp: Supertouch were back on an Amnesty bill in August 1990, at the Ritz with Killing Time, Token Entry, Sick of It All, Gorilla Biscuits, Burn, Quicksand and Vision.

years.src: Revelation Records · Some Will Never Know
years.h: The Earth Is Flat comes out as Revelation REV 21
years.p: Supertouch's only album of their first run: eleven songs, from Engine to Shame. How Do You Feel, first played in Connecticut in 1988, becomes their signature song.
years.xp:
Revelation's writeup calls the record ahead of its time. The band had been pushing hardcore toward quiet parts, major chords and improvisation, and here it shows.

Biviano says they knew How Do You Feel was a gamble the first time they played it: "a song that had a quiet intro, and a quiet middle part."

eras.title: A tour van, a carpeted stage and a shelved album
eras.text: With a new rhythm section, Supertouch toured Europe and kept writing, but the '90s wore them down. They quit in 1996 with a second album, Guide to the Stars, finished and unreleased.

years.cap: Supertouch live in a packed room, singer Mark Ryan in the crowd, around 1991
yt: Full set at the Marquee, New York, February 21, 1992
years.h: Bradford to Ieper overnight, then bed down on the stage
years.p: On a European tour, Supertouch play Bradford, England, load straight into the van for the Dover ferry, and arrive late at Vort'n Vis in Ieper, Belgium. They sleep on its carpeted stage.
years.xp:
The October to December 1992 tour was booked by Navigator, and Ieper was the band's only Belgian show. The line-up was Mark Ryan, Jon Biviano, drummer Rich Edsell and bassist Mark Randall.

The club fed them after the set and handed out Duvel, which Biviano says he still connects with Ieper.

years.h: Utah police arrest a Supertouch bassist on tour
years.p: Jon Biviano says the band's bass player was arrested in Utah in 1993 on drug paraphernalia charges.
years.xp: Biviano says the evidence was a bowl in the bassist's backpack that an officer claimed smelled like marijuana. His verdict: "Total bullshit." He names no one.

years.big: "I would have fought a lot harder to make sure Supertouch didn't stop."
years.src: Some Will Never Know · Supertouch Bandcamp
yt: Full set at the Tune Inn, New Haven, December 2, 1995
years.h: Supertouch quit, with Guide to the Stars unreleased
years.p: Jon Biviano on 1996. The band's second album, Guide to the Stars, stays unreleased for well over a decade.
years.xp:
Biviano went on to Windfall, a band with a female singer, from 1999 to 2003, and joined Running Like Thieves in 2000.

When Supertouch came back in 2010, the band tied it to historical releases, including Guide to the Stars.

eras.title: A surprise set at the Bowl
eras.text: A walk-on at the Black N' Blue Bowl turned into a real reunion: new songs, a 7", the old WNYU tape on vinyl, and the big hardcore festivals.

years.cap: Mark Ryan singing in the crowd at Irving Plaza, Revelation Records 25th Anniversary Show, New York, October 14, 2012
years.h: A walk-on at the Black N' Blue Bowl restarts Supertouch
years.p: Fourteen years after they stopped, the band plays an unannounced set in New York, and Mark Ryan and Jon Biviano decide to keep going.

years.h: Lost My Way is the first new Supertouch in two decades
years.p: Four songs on Reaper Records, with Mark Ryan and Jon Biviano joined by Rich Edsell on drums and Dean Baltulonis on bass.

years.h: The WNYU tape, 23 years on, finally on vinyl
years.p: Supertouch's St. Patrick's Day 1988 set, a traded cassette for 23 years, comes out through Horror Hotel.

years.h: Late-'80s songs go to America's Hardcore Fest in Cambridge
years.p: Supertouch bring the old songs to Cambridge, Massachusetts, as the reunion's last show we could find.
